newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: RODAMCO SEES H2 CLEARLY HIGHER THAN H1.
newsitem.headline: RODAMCO SEES H2 CLEARLY HIGHER THAN H1.

text.p: Property investment fund Rodamco NV said it expected a net profit per share in the second half of the financial year 1996/97 which would clearly exceed the 1.30 guilders posted in the first half of the year.
"This is caused by the large investments that Rodamco has made in recent months," the company said in a statement.
It added that the favourable effect of these investments would not entirely compensate for the decrease in the first half of the year when net profits fell 6.25 percent to 212 million guilders.
Rodamco therefore reiterated its forecast that 1996/97 full-year net would be slightly lower than the 446 million guilders posted in the previous year.
The previously announced buy-back of sales was proceeding according to plan, Rodamco said.
Up to now, it has bought back 3.4 million of its own shares and an additional 2.5 million will be bought before the end of the financial year.
Rodamco said its recent investments were expected to raise its profits per share to about three guilders in 1997/98. Last year it posted a 2.80 guilders net per share.
It said that from March of this year it had invested a total of 1.8 billion guilders in new property and had sold investments for a total of almost 400 million guilders.

Currently, Rodamco has another 500 million guilders available to be invested. It plans to do so because the interest gains on cash assets is considerably lower than the net yield on new investments, given the low interest rates.
"Consequently, each cash penny we invest will result in a further improvement in our profit prospects," Rodamco chairman Sjeng Kremers commented in the company's statement.
